claims.text: A hybrid ML free-energy method can accurately reproduce solid-phase free energies near melting.
A hybrid ML free-energy method can accurately reproduce liquid-phase free energies near melting.
The hybrid method can reproduce fusion properties at a fraction of the cost of full ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
The proposed ML potential will be calibrated against a limited set of ab initio free-energy evaluations.
Targeted perturbative corrections will account for anharmonic effects and electron–vibration coupling.
The proposed corrections will keep the solid and liquid free energies faithful to ab initio standards.
The method is intended for elemental and binary systems from approximately 50 K below to 100 K above their melting temperatures.
Multicomponent high-entropy systems are initially excluded from the method's claimed domain.
The ML potential captures the dominant interatomic interactions and associated vibrational contributions.
Correction terms provide a bridge between the ML surrogate and the full ab initio description.
Sparse, representative ab initio training allows the lower-cost model to interpolate free energies over the relevant temperature range.
Explicit entropy-related corrections prevent the loss of anharmonic and electron–vibration effects.
Retaining anharmonic and electron–vibration effects preserves phase fidelity.
The hybrid method should predict phase free energies and melting points with less than 5% deviation from full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The hybrid method should reduce computational time by approximately one order of magnitude.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics and TOR-TILD results provide benchmark high-temperature free energies and thermodynamic properties for elemental and binary systems.
Transferability beyond binary systems is uncertain because more complex systems have more complicated interaction effects.

The hypothesis is falsified if free energies or melting points differ by more than 5% from ab initio molecular-dynamics results, or if cost is not reduced by roughly an order of magnitude relative to the reference workflows.
